label: v0.2
notes:

- One finger flies the aircraft: it moves with your finger, never jumps to it. Shooting is automatic.
- A safe start, then a Razor enters: its eye flashes before every dart, so you can see it coming and slide away.
- HEALTH 30: each dart costs 10, with a short safe moment after a hit. Only the small bright core in the cockpit can be hit.
- ABILITY (bottom-left): Sunpunch, a local solar blast, ready at launch, 12 s cooldown. SUPER (bottom-right): charges from kills (early version).
- Pause, clear defeat reason, one-tap Replay (instant), steering sensitivity in Settings.
- Arabic and English. Shapes and sounds are temporary: the real look arrives in the next milestone.

label: v0.3
notes:
SUNPUNCH v0.3 — the first polished combat slice (real look and sound)
- Real art: the orange Spark, the cobalt Razors, the shell boulder and the Midnight Reef islands scroll by under the crescent moon.
- Collect mint stars to power up during the flight: FLIGHT LV 2 side cannons, LV 3 floating cannons + tracking rockets, LV 4 the solar laser (keeps everything). Every flight starts at LV 1.
- Shell boulders drift down from 18 s: shoot them for stars, don't fly into them.
- Weapons kick back when they fire, enemies flash when hit, Razors snap their wings when destroyed; a short freeze shows what hit you.
- New sound: every weapon, hit, warning, pickup and level-up, plus the Reef Run music. The Razor's charge warning stays audible over your own fire.
- Sunpunch (ABILITY) has its real solar-orb look; Daystar (SUPER) is still the early version.
- New setting: Reduced effects (calmer flashes and shake; threats never change).

label: v0.4
notes:
SUNPUNCH v0.4: the whole Reef Run, from launch to Big Bite's defeat
- **The full mission:** about 100 seconds through Midnight Reef. Razors open, then Puff, Claw, a shell boulder and a salvage pod arrive. After them come a needle spire, the Razor three-burst, Puff's double fan, a Razor gate, Claw's comb and the three-enemy wave, with calm moments to collect in between.
- **New enemies:**
  - Puff swells, then fires slow magenta spheres in a fan.
  - Claw glows, then fires crimson capsules from its left claw, then its right.
  - Each is taught alone first; in the wave they take turns, and at most two attacks come at you at once.
- **New obstacles:**
  - The salvage pod breaks for +10 coins.
  - The needle spire and the Razor gate end the run if you touch them.
  - Both are announced with a red marker before they arrive, and the gate always keeps a wide, steady opening.
- **Big Bite, the boss:**
  - Its armour blocks your shots; hit the glowing core while its mouth is open.
  - It fires fin volleys, a mouth fan, and Furnace Breath: a warned flame lane you must leave, which costs 20 HEALTH.
  - At half health it transforms once into INFERNO, with heavier guns, two fans and two flame pulses.
- **Victory:** Big Bite's jaw splits and its coins pour out. The results show your clear time, coins and wallet, with Replay first. Coins you collect are kept, even if you lose.
- **Sound:** new sounds for every new enemy, obstacle and boss attack. Big Bite and Inferno have their own music, and there is a victory theme.
- **Look:** the reef edges are now separate, varied pillars, and the moon finally looks like a moon.

label: v0.5
notes:
SUNPUNCH v0.5: four aircraft to earn, a hangar, a map and progress that is never lost
- **Four permanent aircraft:** Spark, Striker, Phoenix and Helios. Each new one has more HEALTH (30, 40, 50, 60), hits harder, and fights differently from FLIGHT LV 2:
  - Striker's rail cannons swing in and lock onto the enemy in front of you.
  - Phoenix's two pods pick their own targets, or both hit the same one.
  - Helios's rail shots go through one enemy and hit the next.
  - Every aircraft changes at each flight level, and every flight still starts at LV 1.
- **Daystar on every aircraft:** the armour lifts and three heavy volleys fire (plasma spears, solar pulses, paired rockets) for six seconds. Good play now charges it about 50 seconds into a run.
- **New screens:**
  - **Campaign:** your aircraft, Juno, your coins and one PLAY button.
  - **Midnight Reef map:** Stage 01 ready to launch; five future islands are shown locked as "Future update".
  - **Upgrade hangar:** see the next aircraft, what it adds, your coins and exactly how many you still need, then buy it.
  - **Reveal:** buying plays a short "assemble, ignite, yours" moment you can skip, then lets you fly the new aircraft.
- **Coins and goals:**
  - Every coin counts the moment you collect it and is saved within two seconds, even if you lose, restart or quit.
  - Puffs and Claws now drop coins.
  - Four one-time bonuses, each shown with its reason.
  - Results show how far you got and exactly how many coins the next aircraft still needs.
- **Safe progress:**
  - The game keeps a backup save and recovers from a damaged one with a message.
  - Coins and aircraft are never lost or charged twice, and a purchase is all or nothing.
  - If the app is closed mid-flight, your collected coins stay and the game tells you.
- **Fairer boss:** Big Bite can't be melted in seconds by the stronger aircraft. Every aircraft now gets a real fight of about 30 to 36 seconds.
- **Sound and music:** new hangar music, sounds for every aircraft's side weapons, its own Daystar sound, and sounds for the map, hangar, purchase and reveal.

label: v0.6
notes:
SUNPUNCH v0.6: a living boss, the new Spark, music that follows the run, comfort options and performance work (release candidate)
- **Big Bite is alive:** no more picture swaps. Its jaw really hinges open and snaps, the solar core charges and flashes white on every hit, the fins sway, the eyes and head follow you, and it rears back before the Furnace fire (a full second of warning). At half health you watch it transform into Inferno (plates split, horns rise, barrels swing out, fire), and at the end the core ruptures and the jaw splits into a wreck.
- **The new Spark:** your approved Spark design is now in the game. It grows a little bigger and better at every FLIGHT LV; new hardware slides out first, then the ship settles, with a warm ignition glow. Daystar unfolds with real moving parts on every aircraft.
- **Enemies break apart** in their own way when destroyed, and the reef light tells the story: warm at the start, darker toward Big Bite, warm again after you win.
- **Music that follows the run:** a calm start, rising pressure, a hush before the boss, the boss and Inferno themes, and a short results piece after a loss. More variety in the most frequent sounds.
- **Fairer, clearer fights:**
  - Red edge arrows warn before spires, gates, side attacks and Big Bite's fin volley (now a 0.9-second warning).
  - Big Bite starts a little gentler for its first 10 seconds; stronger aircraft now beat it faster.
  - Collecting stars also charges Daystar a little, and the button pulses when it's ready.
  - Daystar lights up the reef in gold with heavier spears.
- **Losing helps you:** the defeat card shows what got you, a tip, how far you got and one next goal. Replay is back in flight in about one second.
- **Comfort settings:** master mute, Reduced flashes and Reduced shake as separate switches, Larger text, vibration off everywhere, and "Replay first-flight tips". Text is checked to fit on small phones in English and Arabic.
- **Performance work for budget phones:** phones now use the lighter renderer we chose, hidden full-screen layers are gone, graphics and sounds load before the flight, and the game thread does less work per frame. The busiest moments still dip below a steady 60 on the cheapest phones; more work follows.
- **Release candidate:** no developer tools in the player build; full test suite run after the last change; handover pack written.
- Striker, Phoenix and Helios keep their current look until their new designs are approved.

label: v0.7
notes:
SUNPUNCH v0.7: the whole of Midnight Reef, four aircraft worth wanting, a living Big Bite (internal candidate)
- **Ten levels instead of one:** Midnight Reef is now a full sector of ten levels, from the warm entrance to Big Bite's Maw. Each level adds one new idea (Puff fans, breakable walls, Claw rhythm, spires, formations...) and teaches it on its own first. Level 1 is open; each clear opens the next, and every cleared level can be flown again.
- **A real campaign map:** scroll up a painted chain of floating islands. Your current level glows orange, a tapped level gets a light ring, and the card shows the level, its length and your best. Three more sectors (Ember Shoals, Wreck Field, The Drop-off) wait above the clouds, clearly locked and "coming in a future update".
- **Aircraft you want next:** the hangar shows the next aircraft in the spotlight while Juno builds it on her workbench as your coins come in. Try it in a short test flight before you buy. Buying plays a short reveal (parts lock in, engines ignite, YOURS), which you can skip.
- **Every aircraft grows four times in a flight:** Spark, Striker, Phoenix and Helios each have their own look and weapons at every FLIGHT LV, and their own Daystar transformation. Striker clears the same fight about 16-18 % faster than Spark.
- **Big Bite is alive:** it watches you, opens its jaw to show the core, transforms into Inferno at half health, and breaks apart with a burst of coins.
- **Enemies with character:** Razors bank and aim before they fire, Puffs swell before a fan, Claws swing left and right; each breaks apart in its own way.
- **A new flight screen:** a segmented HEALTH bar, a FLIGHT LV bar with MAX, a slim tracker showing how far you are through the level (Big Bite's icon only in Level 10), and new Sunpunch and Daystar buttons.
- **Rewards for ten levels:** later levels pay more, every level has a one-time first-clear bonus, and finishing the sector pays a bonus. Helios now costs 1,100 coins.
- **Menus redone:** home, pause, settings, level clear, sector complete and defeat cards match the new style, in English and Arabic. Clearing a level now opens its own LEVEL CLEAR card, and beating Big Bite opens SECTOR COMPLETE.
- **A darker, clearer battlefield:** a painted cloud channel runs behind your lane, so shots, coins and enemies stand out.
- **Still to come (honest):** the Sunpunch blast is close but not yet at our quality bar; Spark, Phoenix and Helios share one level-up sound (Striker has its own); on our test phones (Galaxy A55/A56, Pixel 9/10) the game holds 60 fps or more, with one short hiccup left when Big Bite turns into Inferno on the Galaxy phones; iPhone not measured yet. Level 1 can feel empty near its end if you clear it fast (we tune that next). This is an internal candidate: no outside players have tried it yet.
- **Art spend (internal):** Sunpunch sprites 96 and the lane cloud 80 Scenario credits on our own style model; the boss wreck and the parked Spark were made with OpenAI (2 low drafts + 1 final each).

# SUNPUNCH v0.23: what changed

- The Super lasts much longer now (6 to 7.5 seconds, longer for stronger aircraft families) and ends with one big closing volley.
- The power buttons have no words any more: a clenching sun-fist and your aircraft family's own wings show charging, ready, active and cooldown.
- An arcade announcer calls your powers ("SUNPUNCH!", each family's Super call, "RAGE!"); you can switch the voice off in Settings.
- Harder levels: obstacles and enemies now come together, with up to 4 obstacle types per level (2 on Level 1, 3 on Level 2).
- One clean warning style: a lit lane or footprint shows where danger comes and fills up until it arrives. Warnings that touch now draw as one shape instead of piling on each other.
- RAGE: if a fight drags on, the enemies get angry, attack nonstop and finally dive at you one by one, and the level ends within about 3 minutes; you can't hide in one spot forever. In normal play you will rarely meet it (about 1 run in 25).
- Brood Tides no longer hold a level up: when the wave is beaten the tide winds down and swims away, so Levels 2 and 3 keep moving.
- Enemies and obstacles crowd each other less: fewer ships sit on top of each other on Levels 6 and 10.
- Bigger enemies now get to show their attack before they fall, and early enemies are tougher and attack sooner.
- Restored full-quality art from earlier versions (aircraft paint, boss textures, flight sprites).

Honest note: the new warnings and power buttons read better than before but are still below our own look bar; busy moments are not yet as clean as we want, obstacles and enemies don't mix as much as we want on every level, and small enemies (razors, puffs, claws) still often fall before they attack. Level 9 can still turn to RAGE in about one run in five. The Home screen is being checked again on a real phone. We keep working on all of these.

Honest note on the art: the new power buttons and warnings read better than before but are still below our own 4.5 look bar, and the obstacles of the new levels are too (new obstacle art, stones and menus improved, still below the bar). The full-quality art of earlier versions is restored; the 3-D Big Bite body stays switched off for now. We keep improving all of it.

Honest note on the art:
- the two power buttons show a clenching sun-fist and your aircraft's own wings, with the state shown by (still below our art bar)
- the new warning style (a lit lane or footprint) is clearer than before and is still being polished toward (still below our art bar)
- the obstacles of the new levels look better but are still below our own look bar (still below our art bar)
- 1 finished look item(s) without a passing look check yet
- 1078 art files still use the earlier look without a passing look check
- parts of the look are still below our own 4.5 bar; it keeps improving in the next versions

# SUNPUNCH v0.24: what changed

- Fixed: on smaller phones the level-up banner no longer covers the "drag to move" tip; it now appears just below it.
- Levels 11, 17 and 18 are hard again (they had become a little easier than in 0.22).
- Danger warnings are now checked on every level, including when RAGE is at its strongest.
- A correction to the 0.23 notes: about 6 in 10 enemies get to show their attack before they fall (not yet all of them), and busy moments still look less clean than in 0.22. We keep working on both.

Honest note on the art: the same as v0.23 (the power buttons, warnings and new obstacles read better but are still below our own look bar; the Big Bite boss will be remade so it looks and feels better).

Honest note on the art:
- 1078 art files still use the earlier look without a passing look check
- parts of the look are still below our own 4.5 bar; it keeps improving in the next versions

label: v0.25
notes:
# SUNPUNCH v0.25: what changed

## New
- Big Bite (Level 10) is remade as a real 3D shark: its jaw opens at the natural joint, it dives through the field, and it has new attacks (a lunge pair, dive and surface, a triple bite with Gunlets, a 5-bite last stand). It has the same health as before but hits much harder: a good player takes several times more hits than in 0.24.
- Coil the dragon (Level 20) is one big 3D dragon: the holes burst and merge into one, the dragon climbs out and fills the screen, and it rears up and breathes across the screen when it gets angry.
- Both bosses have their own new music theme and new sounds (arrival, attacks, dives, hits, defeat).
- Sector 2 weapons look like a welding war (heat beams, sparks, glowing rivets) and are harder; Sector 1 levels 3-10 are a step harder.
- Most enemies (over 9 in 10) show their attack before they fall, none leaves the screen without a fight, and obstacle walls almost never come without enemies.
- Level 1 opens with a row of star shells to break.
- A new Store, a smaller but richer launch sheet, a Home button on the Map that looks like a button, and new power buttons. The power tab is gone.
- The upgrade moment on Home keeps its burst going and flashes, in English and Arabic.
- The crane obstacle shows what it will do before it swings; warnings are cleaner.
- The art is back at full quality (the app is about 360 MB).

## Fixed
- The RAGE hunter hurt you from anywhere on screen; now only when it touches you.
- Big Bite's Gunlets could hide inside its jaw.
- Coil played Big Bite's music; it now has its own.
- A slowdown on Home after visiting the hangar (memory use cut by more than half).

## Honest notes
- Not checked on a real phone this version (smoothness and phone start-up): tell us if anything stutters or will not start.
- Sector 2 is clearly harder than in 0.24 (our test pilots clear about 4 in 10 runs instead of 6 in 10), and Level 18 is the hardest: our test pilots did not clear it at all. Tell us if it feels unfair.
- Coil (Level 20) is not harder than in 0.24 for a skilled player; the harder boss work went into Big Bite this time.
- The optional download pack for extra art is not ready yet, so all the art is inside the app (nothing was cut to make it smaller).
- The game stays at 20 levels and 2 bosses this version: Sectors 3 and 4 and their bosses (Kiln Mantis, Mother Lure) are not coming.
